sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Midland, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Midland has an active energy-driven economy, and homes there can move to investors, landlords and cash buyers quickly when the price reflects condition. The tradeoff is the usual one: speed and certainty versus the top possible price.

Ask every buyer how long a written offer stays open, and compare the offers side by side.

sections.h2: What does the Midland economy mean for sellers?
sections.html:
Midland calls itself the heart of the Permian Basin, and its fact sheet lists Chevron, Diamondback Energy, Midland ISD, Midland Health, the city itself and H-E-B among major employers. ConocoPhillips, ExxonMobil, EOG Resources, Oxy and AST SpaceMobile also have headquarters or regional campuses there.

The city reports a metro population of 193,139 for 2026, growth of 8.1 percent from 2020 to 2026, a median age of 31.5 and an unemployment rate of 3.1 percent. It also states that per capita income ranks second highest in the United States. Its own FAQ notes that apartment rents are rising while occupancy has improved, which is relevant if your buyer is an investor.

  • Midland International Air and Space Port serves American, Delta, Southwest and United.
  • The city runs a Midland Development Corporation that offers business incentives.
  • Midland College and Midland ISD are the main education institutions named by the city.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Midland house fast?
sections.html:
Most sellers choose between a listing, a direct cash sale, and a sale to a local investor. Pick based on the house, not on a headline price.

  • List with an agent. Best for move-in-ready houses in a stable market segment; you carry repairs, showings and financing risk.
  • Cash buyer. Works for houses with foundation, roof, plumbing or electrical problems, and for owners relocating on short notice.
  • Investor sale with a leaseback or short close. Useful if you need time to move out.
  • Hold and rent. Only practical if you can handle repairs and tenant turnover from a distance.

Ask for each offer in writing and compare what you would net after fees, repairs and carrying costs.

sections.h2: What permits matter before selling a Midland house?
sections.html:
Midland requires a residential building permit for new construction, additions, remodeling, repairs and detached accessory buildings. The permit must be pulled by the property owner or a licensed and bonded contractor registered with the city.

Work must start within 180 days of issue, and it expires if construction stops for more than 180 days. Residential permit requests go by email to the permit clerk, with a 25 percent fee at submission and the remaining 75 percent at approval; plan review usually takes about 5 to 7 business days. If you did unpermitted work, a buyer's inspector may ask for it to be documented, so ask the city planning or permit office how to handle it. The city building permits page has the current process.

Short-term rentals matter too: the city requires anyone running a hotel, including a short-term rental, to collect a hotel occupancy tax of seven percent of the price paid.

sections.h2: What property tax relief applies to Midland homes?
sections.html:
Midland homeowners get school-district homestead relief plus local options. The Midland Central Appraisal District lists the amounts for each taxing unit, which matters to a buyer reading your tax history.

Source: Midland CAD current exemptions. A disabled veteran may receive between $5,000 and $12,000 off assessed value depending on rating, and a 100 percent rating exempts the full homesteadable value. Apply with Form 50-114 or through the district.

sections.h2: What if my Midland house has a tenant or squatter?
sections.html:
An occupant who is a tenant must be removed through eviction, while a person who entered without permission may fall under a faster process. Texas requires a written notice to vacate of at least three days unless the lease says otherwise, then a justice court suit. The hearing is set no sooner than 10 and no later than 21 days after filing.

For someone who is not a family member or current or former tenant, Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner file a request for removal with the sheriff or constable without a court case. The conditions include that the person stayed after being told to leave and that no suit is pending between the two of you. A wrongful removal can expose the owner to a lawsuit, so confirm each condition with the sheriff's office first.

  • A writ of possession cannot be issued more than 60 days after judgment, though a court may allow 90 days for good cause.
  • Cash buyers often accept occupied homes, which saves you the wait.

sections.h2: What should Midland sellers prepare before taking offers?
sections.html:
A short checklist keeps surprises out of closing. Collect the paperwork now and the title company will move faster later.

  • Your deed and any mortgage payoff statement.
  • The latest tax bill and any homestead exemption notice from the appraisal district.
  • Permit records for remodels, repairs or detached buildings.
  • Lease and rent roll if the house is tenant-occupied.
  • Any water, roof or foundation reports you have.

Midland's permitting process uses email submission, so keep scanned copies of old permits where you can find them. If you cannot locate a permit, call the permit clerk at 432-685-7390 for guidance.

sections.h2: What does Midland's own growth plan say about the city?
sections.html:
The city's strategic plan lists six goals: more quality jobs, a safe and secure city, quality of life and place, clear communication, sound fiscal management, and stronger infrastructure. It also points to a Vision Midland story map covering capital projects, parks, downtown redevelopment and economic zones.

For a seller, those projects matter only as context. Street, drainage or downtown work near your address can change how buyers see the block, so ask the city's planning office what is scheduled near you. The city's fact sheet says sales tax collections grew 54.63 percent from fiscal 2015 to 2025, and that high-income households earning $200,000 or more grew 20.4 percent between 2023 and 2024. Those figures describe the local economy, not any one home's value, so rely on written offers and an agent's comparable sales for pricing.

sections.h2: When are Texas property taxes due and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed around October 1 and are delinquent after January 31. Penalty and interest start on February 1: six percent penalty plus one percent interest, rising by one percent a month.

A tax lien attaches on January 1, so the January 1 owner is liable for that year. Title companies normally prorate the bill and pay it from your proceeds. Owners protest value by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever is later. The Comptroller's calendar lists each step.

sections.h2: How are deeds and inherited Midland houses handled?
sections.html:
The county clerk records deeds in the county where the property sits, and the instrument must be signed and acknowledged. Inherited property needs proof of who may convey: an administrator's deed, a muniment of title order, a transfer on death deed with an affidavit of death, or, as a last resort, an affidavit of heirship.

Small estates may use an affidavit if assets other than homestead are $75,000 or less and all heirs agree. Probate a will within four years of death. See the State Law Library guide.

sections.h2: What should I ask a Midland cash buyer?
sections.html: Ask who the buyer is, whether the offer is for the whole house as-is, and where earnest money will be held. Ask how many days the buyer needs to close and what happens if the title search turns up a lien. Request the contract before you commit, and have the title company, not the buyer, prepare the closing statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Midland house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers regularly buy houses as they stand, including ones with foundation, roof or plumbing issues. Expect the offer to reflect repair cost.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for repairs in Midland?
faqs.a: Yes, for repairs, remodels, additions and detached accessory buildings. The owner or a bonded contractor registered with the city must apply, and permits expire if work does not start within 180 days.

faqs.q: What homestead exemptions can a Midland buyer claim?
faqs.a: Midland ISD gives $140,000 plus a 10 percent local option, per the appraisal district's table. A buyer closing after January 1 may claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller did not.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax bill at closing?
faqs.a: Taxes are normally prorated and paid from your proceeds by the title company. The lien attaches January 1, so confirm the split in the closing statement.

faqs.q: What happens if I inherit a house in Midland?
faqs.a: You will need court or recorded documents proving who can sign. Options include a muniment of title, administration, a transfer on death deed or an affidavit of heirship.
